title: Policy Information
text:
GENERAL RETAIL LENDING CREDIT POLICY
Policy Reference: CRP-GL-001
Policy Owner: Credit Risk Department
Version: 1.0
Classification: Internal Policy Manual
Currency: United States Dollars (USD)

title: Purpose and Scope
text:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy establishes the standards and procedures governing the assessment, approval, rejection
and review of general retail loan applications. Its purpose is to ensure that lending decisions are
consistent, prudent, transparent and supported by an applicant's verified financial circumstances.
The policy applies to individual applicants seeking retail credit for permitted purposes. Additional
requirements may apply to specific loan products, purposes, amounts and repayment tenures.
All monetary amounts in this policy are expressed in United States dollars (USD).

title: Applicant Eligibility and Verification
text: 2. Applicant Eligibility and Verification

title: Legal Eligibility
text:
2.1 Legal Eligibility
Applicants must satisfy the applicable legal age of 18 years and above, contractual capacity and
residency requirements for the credit product concerned.

title: Identity and Documentation
text:
2.2 Identity and Documentation
Applicants must provide valid identity documentation and all information reasonably required to
assess the application, including income, employment, monthly expenses, existing liabilities and
requested loan details.

title: Verification Requirements
text:
2.3 Verification Requirements
Material information must be verified using appropriate documentation or approved verification
procedures. Applications containing material inconsistencies, suspected misrepresentation or
unresolved information gaps must be referred for further assessment.
An application must not be declined solely because information is temporarily unavailable where the
matter can reasonably be resolved through clarification or additional documentation.

title: Creditworthiness and Repayment History
text: 3. Creditworthiness and Repayment History

title: Credit Score Assessment
text:
3.1 Credit Score Assessment
Credit score is a principal consideration in assessing an applicant's creditworthiness.
The following standards apply to the standard assessment process:
•
Credit score of 650 or above: Meets the minimum credit-score standard, subject to the
remaining eligibility and affordability requirements.
•
Credit score from 600 to 649: Requires enhanced assessment and manual review.
•
Credit score below 600: Normally results in decline under the standard lending criteria. An
exception may be considered only where permitted by the authorised exception process.
Meeting the minimum credit-score standard does not guarantee approval.

title: Credit History
text:
3.2 Credit History
The bank shall consider available information regarding previous repayment performance, overdue
obligations, defaults and other material adverse credit events.
Significant adverse repayment history may result in decline or enhanced review, depending on the
severity, recency and circumstances of the event.

title: Incomplete Credit History
text:
3.3 Incomplete Credit History
Where an applicant has insufficient credit history to support a reliable assessment, the application
shall be evaluated using other verified financial information and referred for manual review where
necessary.

title: Income and Financial Stability
text: 4. Income and Financial Stability

title: Income Verification
text:
4.1 Income Verification
Applicants must demonstrate a verifiable and reasonably stable source of income sufficient to
support the proposed credit obligation.
Acceptable income sources may include employment income, self-employment earnings and other
lawful, verifiable recurring income.

title: Income Reference Standard
text:
4.2 Income Reference Standard
Annual verified income of $30,000 is the standard reference level for general retail lending
assessment.
Applications below this level require enhanced assessment of the requested amount, repayment
tenure, essential living expenses and remaining repayment capacity. Lower income alone shall not be
treated as proof of inability to repay where the applicable product criteria permit consideration of
other evidence.

title: Income Stability
text:
4.3 Income Stability
The bank shall assess the continuity, reliability and verifiability of the applicant's income. Where
income is irregular, recently commenced or insufficiently documented, additional evidence may be
required before a final decision is made.

title: Existing Financial Commitments and Affordability
text: 5. Existing Financial Commitments and Affordability

title: Expense-to-Income Assessment
text:
5.1 Expense-to-Income Assessment
The bank shall assess the proportion of gross monthly income committed to the applicant's reported
monthly expenses and existing financial obligations.
Expense-to-Income Ratio (%) = (Total Monthly Expenses / Gross Monthly Income) × 100
The standard assessment bands are:
•
Up to 40%: Generally acceptable, subject to the remaining criteria.
•
Above 40% and up to 60%: Requires enhanced affordability assessment and manual review.
•
Above 60%: Normally results in decline unless a documented exception is authorised.
The assessment must consider whether the applicant retains sufficient income to meet essential
living costs and the proposed repayment obligation.

title: Remaining Monthly Income
text:
5.2 Remaining Monthly Income
Remaining monthly income is calculated as follows:
Remaining Monthly Income = Gross Monthly Income − Total Monthly Expenses
The applicant must demonstrate sufficient remaining income to support the proposed repayment.
•
Positive remaining income is necessary but not sufficient for approval.
•
Zero or negative remaining income triggers additional assessment.
•
If the shortfall is confirmed and no adequate repayment capacity can be established, the
application shall normally be declined.

title: Proposed Loan Repayment Affordability
text:
5.3 Proposed Loan Repayment Affordability
The bank shall assess the proposed monthly repayment in relation to the applicant's remaining
monthly income.
Repayment-to-Surplus Ratio (%) = (Proposed Monthly Loan Repayment / Remaining Monthly
Income) × 100
Where remaining monthly income is positive, the following standards apply:
•
Up to 30%: Generally acceptable on this criterion.
•
Above 30% and up to 50%: Requires manual review.
•
Above 50%: Normally results in decline or escalation for an authorised exception.
Where remaining monthly income is zero or negative, this ratio must not be calculated as an ordinary
percentage measure. The application must be assessed under Clause 5.2.

title: Repayment Calculation
text:
5.4 Repayment Calculation
The proposed monthly repayment shall be calculated using the applicable interest rate, repayment
tenure and repayment structure.
A principal-only estimate shall not be treated as the contractual monthly instalment where interest
or other applicable charges affect the repayment amount.

title: Existing Debt Relative to Income
text:
5.5 Existing Debt Relative to Income
Existing indebtedness shall be assessed relative to annual verified income.
Outstanding Debt-to-Income Ratio (%) = (Total Outstanding Debt / Annual Gross Income) × 100
The following bands apply as supporting indicators:
•
Up to 30%: Generally acceptable as a supporting indicator.
•
Above 30% and up to 50%: Requires closer assessment of existing obligations and
repayment capacity.
•
Above 50%: Requires heightened scrutiny and documented assessment.
These bands do not independently determine the final decision. The bank shall consider the nature
of the liabilities, current repayment obligations and the applicant's overall financial position.

title: Existing Loan Exposure
text:
5.6 Existing Loan Exposure
Total existing loan amount relative to annual income shall be assessed as an additional indicator of
credit exposure.
Existing Loan Amount-to-Income Ratio (%) = (Total Existing Loan Amount / Annual Gross Income) ×
100
Ratios above 50% require additional scrutiny of the applicant's existing obligations and proposed
borrowing. This indicator shall not be used as an automatic rejection criterion without considering
repayment capacity and other relevant circumstances.

title: Requested Loan Amount and Tenure
text: 6. Requested Loan Amount and Tenure

title: Loan Amount
text:
6.1 Loan Amount
The requested amount must be consistent with the applicant's verified financial position and ability
to repay.
The bank shall consider annual income, existing liabilities, remaining monthly income, proposed
repayment, loan purpose and requested tenure when assessing the amount.
No application shall be approved solely because the requested amount falls within a general income-
based range.

title: Requested Loan-to-Income Ratio
text:
6.2 Requested Loan-to-Income Ratio
The requested loan-to-income ratio may be used as a supporting indicator.
Requested Loan-to-Income Ratio (%) = (Requested Loan Amount / Annual Gross Income) × 100
This ratio shall not independently determine approval or rejection. The bank shall assess it alongside
repayment capacity, existing obligations and the proposed tenure.

title: Repayment Tenure
text:
6.3 Repayment Tenure
The proposed tenure must fall within the permitted terms of the applicable credit product. The
repayment schedule must be assessed to determine whether the resulting instalments are
affordable.
Where the requested amount or tenure produces an unaffordable repayment obligation, the
application shall be declined or referred for review, as appropriate.

title: Credit Decision Standards
text: 7. Credit Decision Standards

title: Approval
text:
7.1 Approval
An application may be approved where:
1. The applicant satisfies the applicable legal and documentation requirements.
2. Creditworthiness is acceptable under the bank's standards.
3. Income and material financial information have been adequately verified.
4. Repayment capacity satisfies the applicable affordability requirements.
5. The requested amount and tenure are permitted for the relevant product.
6. No unresolved material risk concern or mandatory review requirement remains.

title: Rejection
text:
7.2 Rejection
An application shall normally be declined where a material policy requirement is not met and the
deficiency cannot be resolved through clarification, additional evidence or an authorised exception.
Grounds for rejection may include:
•
Credit score below the standard minimum, subject to the exception process.
•
Confirmed inability to meet the proposed repayment from available income.
•
Excessive expense burden or indebtedness under the applicable standards.
•
Ineligibility for the requested product or repayment tenure.
•
Material misrepresentation or failure to satisfy mandatory verification requirements.
The recorded reason for rejection must identify the applicable policy requirement and the verified
information supporting the decision.

title: Manual Review
text:
7.3 Manual Review
Manual review is required where:
•
Credit score falls within the borderline band.
•
Expense-to-income or repayment-to-surplus ratios fall within a review band.
•
Remaining income is zero or negative.
•
Material financial information is missing, inconsistent or requires clarification.
•
Credit history is insufficient for a reliable assessment.
•
Financial indicators produce conflicting conclusions.
•
An exception is requested or the circumstances are not adequately addressed by this policy.
A referral for review is not, by itself, a rejection.

title: Exceptions and Authorisation
text:
8. Exceptions and Authorisation
Exceptions to standard lending criteria may be considered only where permitted by the bank's
governance arrangements.
Each exception must include:
1. The policy requirement for which an exception is sought.
2. The verified facts and supporting documentation.
3. The rationale for considering the exception.
4. An assessment of the applicant's repayment capacity.
5. The identity of the authorised reviewer and the final determination.
An exception must not be granted solely to achieve an approval target or to bypass a material
affordability concern.

title: Customer Communication
text:
9. Customer Communication
Applicants shall receive clear and accurate communication regarding the outcome of their
application.
Where an application is declined, the explanation should identify the applicable lending requirement
and the relevant applicant information supporting the decision.
Where additional assessment is required, the applicant shall be informed that the decision is pending
review or clarification, rather than being incorrectly told that the application has been declined.
Explanations must not state that an applicant failed a requirement unless the available evidence and
applicable policy clause support that conclusion.

title: Records and Policy Review
text:
10. Records and Policy Review
The bank shall maintain records of the application information, verification performed, applicable
policy requirements, decision rationale, exceptions and final outcome.
This policy shall be reviewed periodically to assess whether its lending standards remain appropriate
and consistent with the bank's risk appetite, product requirements and observed repayment
performance.
Any amendment to a threshold or eligibility requirement must be formally documented, approved by
the authorised policy owner and applied consistently.
End of Policy
